findings.description: 必ず誰かがやってくるわけだから is rendered That is because someone had come there before, replacing a predictable arrival with a past visit and reversing the causal link.

contexts.japanese:
「何しろ焼却炉からは祖父さまの遺体の悪臭だ。
必ず誰かがやってくるわけだから、仕掛けだけ施せば、犯人はその場を離れ、嘉音くんの死亡時刻にアリバイを作ることは充分できる…！」
contexts.japanesePC: 何しろ焼却炉からは祖父さまの遺体の悪臭だ。必ず誰かがやってくるわけだから、仕掛けだけ施せば、犯人はその場を離れ、嘉音くんの死亡時刻にアリバイを作ることは充分できる…！」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「何しろ焼却炉からは祖父さまの遺体の悪臭だ。
必ず誰かがやってくるわけだから、仕掛けだけ施せば、犯人はその場を離れ、嘉音くんの死亡時刻にアリバイを作ることは充分できる…！」
contexts.WH: After all, the stink of Grandfather's body was coming from the incinerator.  That's because someone had come there before, and if they had just set up a trap, it's certainly possible that the culprit could stay away from that place and use the time of Kanon-kun's death to create an alibi...!"
contexts.MG:
"After all, the stink of Grandfather's body was coming from the incinerator.
Someone was bound to go and check, so if the culprit just set up a trap beforehand, they could easily have stayed away from that place and used the time of Kanon-kun's death to create an alibi...!"
contexts.UP:
"After all, the stink of Grandfather's body was coming from the incinerator.
Someone was bound to come, so all the culprit had to do was set up a trap, and it would be more than possible for them to stay away from that place and create an alibi for the time of your death...!"
contexts.note: Both restore predictable future visitor drawn by odor, enabling advance trap and alibi, rather than earlier visitor.

findings.sourceReading: Because the incinerator emits the corpse smell, somebody is certain to come investigate; a culprit can set the trap, leave and establish an alibi at the death time.
findings.alternative: Somebody necessarily visited earlier to place the corpse, but that is not the proposition in this clause, which explains why an unattended trap could attract a victim.

UP preserves the methodological formulation.

「そういうわけじゃねぇ…。
